citation.title: Analysis of electron cyclotron emission with extended electron cyclotron forward modeling
citation.authors: S S Denk, R Fischer, H M Smith, P Helander, O Maj, E Poli, J Stober, U Stroth, W Suttrop, E Westerhof, M Willensdorfer and the ASDEX Upgrade Team

topic: ECE radiation-transport forward modeling for Te profile inference in Bayesian integrated data analysis (IDA) at ASDEX Upgrade.
own_question: Can a relativistic absorption coefficient combined with a Maxwell–Jüttner distribution model ECE shine-through, pseudo radial displacement, and X2/X3 harmonic overlap for routine Te reconstruction?
actual_method_and_evidence: The authors compared radiation-transport models A, A′ and B against calibrated radiometer Trad from selected discharges, averaged over 1 ms. Te was fitted inside IDA, with SOL channels left out of the fit. Additional checks covered radiation drag, wall reflections and O-mode leakage. The paper defines no forecasting or temporal validation split.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: ECE signals do not always map to local cold-resonance Te. Forward modeling can account for down-shifted shine-through and harmonic overlap in offline profile inference.
claim_checks.qualification: The work concerns electron ECE on ASDEX Upgrade with calibrated Trad. It does not address ECEI voltage snapshots, KSTAR, or ion or impurity temperature.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Offline 1 ms averages of 1 MHz radiometer data. No nowcasting and no report-latency analysis.
validation_if_relevant: Comparison with measured Trad, including SOL channels excluded from the fit, on a few shots. The study did not hold out any shots.
forbidden_inferences: ECEI voltages encode calibrated Te in our study
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional single background citation. It could support a caution that raw ECE-type signals need forward modeling to be read as Te. It does not address our target, timing or validation designs.
